items.title: Plozasiran for Severe Hypertriglyceridemia and Risk of Pancreatitis.
items.abstract: Severe hypertriglyceridemia is associated with an increased risk of acute pancreatitis. Plozasiran, a small interfering RNA targeting APOC3 messenger RNA, lowers triglyceride levels and potentially mitigates the risk of acute pancreatitis. In two double-blind, placebo-controlled trials, 757 adults with severe hypertriglyceridemia were randomly assigned in a 2:1 ratio to receive plozasiran (25 mg) or placebo at baseline and at months 3, 6, and 9. These trials had identical designs, end points, and analytic plans. The primary end point was the percent change in the fasting plasma triglyceride level from baseline to month 12. Key secondary end points were the percent change in the fasting triglyceride level from baseline to month 10, a fasting triglyceride level of less than 500 mg per deciliter (5.6 mmol per liter) and less than 150 mg per deciliter (1.7 mmol per liter), the percent change in the fasting serum triglyceride level at month 12 for patients with a baseline triglyceride level of 880 mg per deciliter or greater, and changes in remnant cholesterol and non-HDL cholesterol. A pooled analysis addressed adjudicated acute pancreatitis, incidence, and first-event timing. At month 12, patients in the plozasiran groups had a median triglyceride level that was lower than the baseline level by 79% and 81% in the two trials. These reductions corresponded to a median difference in the plozasiran groups as compared with the placebo groups (placebo-adjusted change) of -45 percentage points (95% confidence interval [CI], -51 to -38) and -47 percentage points (95% CI, -54 to -39). A triglyceride level of less than 500 mg per deciliter at 12 months was reported in 91% and 93% of the patients in the plozasiran groups and in 51% and 50% of those in the placebo groups (P<0.001). The rates of acute pancreatitis were 1 per 100 patient-years with plozasiran and 5 per 100 patient-years with placebo (rate ratio, 0.22; P = 0.008). Adverse events during treatment occurred in 73% of the patients in both the pooled plozasiran and placebo groups. Among patients with severe hypertriglyceridemia, the use of plozasiran resulted in lower triglyceride levels and a lower risk of acute pancreatitis than placebo at 12 months. (Funded by Arrowhead Pharmaceuticals; SHASTA-3 ClinicalTrials.gov number, NCT06347003; SHASTA-4, NCT06347016.).

items.title: Force-Transmission-Enhanced Dual-Modal Piezoelectric Sensing for Monitoring and Analysis of Cardiovascular Health State.
items.abstract: Monitoring and analyzing cardiovascular health status can reduce the incidence and mortality of cardiovascular diseases, yet this is difficult to implement with current technologies due to the limited information dimensions of single-node sensors and poor skin-sensor biomechanical coupling. To address these issues, this work innovatively constructs a flexible piezoelectric sensing pair (FPSP) mainly composed of BTO/P(VDF-TrFE) piezoelectric nanofiber and a force-transfer-enhanced structure, which can simultaneously capture pulsation signals from the brachial artery and heartbeat. Personalized force-transmission layers with different Young's moduli were designed specifically for the pulsation signal characteristics of the brachial artery and heartbeat to increase the sensing area for pulse signals and reduce transmission loss of heartbeat signals, respectively. The acquired dual-modal data contain richer physiological information compared to single-node data, enabling accurate calculation of pulse transit time. In addition, across various neural network architectures, models trained using dual-modal data achieved significantly higher classification accuracy for common cardiovascular diseases than those trained using single-node data, and they also performed excellently in cardiovascular health prediction tasks. This work not only proposes a new strategy for optimizing wearable sensor performance by enhancing biomechanical coupling but also provides a promising technical framework for the precise analysis and continuous monitoring of cardiovascular health.

items.title: Utilizing Coronary Artery Calcification and the COVID-GRAM Score to Predict Critical Illness in COVID-19 Patients.
items.abstract: Coronary artery calcification (CAC), identified on routine chest computed tomography (CT), has been associated with worse outcomes in hospitalized patients with COVID-19. The COVID-GRAM Score is a risk stratification tool developed to predict critical illness in this population. This study compared the predictive performance of CAC identified on chest CT with that of the COVID-GRAM Score for intensive care unit (ICU) admission among hospitalized patients with COVID-19 and evaluated whether combining these measures improved identification of high-risk patients. We hypothesized that CAC would outperform the COVID-GRAM Score. This retrospective cohort study includes 238 adults hospitalized with COVID-19 at a large academic medical center in Milwaukee, Wisconsin, between July 1, 2020, and July 1, 2021. Data were obtained through electronic medical record database queries and chart review. Eligible patients had confirmed COVID-19 infection and no prior history of coronary artery disease. Statistical analyses included descriptive statistics, sensitivity and specificity analyses, and receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve analysis. The mean age was 64  [SD, 15] years, and 46.2% of patients were women. Patients admitted to the ICU had higher mean COVID-GRAM Scores than those not admitted to the ICU (mean [SD], 168 [45.4] vs 150 [44); P = .01). Any CAC was present in 54.2% of ICU-admitted patients compared with 39.1% of patients not admitted to the ICU, and severe CAC was more common among ICU-admitted patients (18.6% vs 5.6%). The area under the ROC curve (AUC) was 0.61 for illness risk score derived from the COVID-GRAM model, compared with 0.58 for any CAC and 0.57 for severe CAC. Composite measures combining CAC and illness risk score did not improve discriminatory performance. Neither the COVID-GRAM Score nor CAC effectively predicted ICU admission among hospitalized patients with COVID-19. Combining CAC with the illness risk score did not significantly improve predictive performance, highlighting the need for more robust risk stratification tools.

items.title: Usability Testing to Improve the User Experience of an Electronic Patient-Reported Outcome System for Chimeric Antigen Receptor T-Cell Therapies.
items.abstract: Treatment with chimeric antigen receptor T-cell (CAR-T) therapies has led to remission in patients with relapsed/refractory hematologic malignancies. However, CAR-T therapies are associated with severe toxicities. An electronic patient-reported outcome (ePRO) system for CAR-T therapies was developed on a digital electronic clinical outcome assessment platform. The system was designed to capture and monitor symptoms and side effects in CAR-T patients within routine clinical care. This study aimed to assess the usability of the ePRO system and use the findings to inform refinements that enhance user experience. Participants were recruited from a previous study and a National Health Service center. In two rounds of online sessions, participants completed a series of tasks, semistructured interviews, cognitive debriefing, and the system usability scale (SUS). Using the Fit between Individual, Task, and Technology framework, we evaluated system usability. Sessions were audiorecorded, transcribed, and analyzed inductively and deductively to generate themes. Fifteen participants, age 18-79 years, evaluated the ePRO system. Qualitative analysis identified eight themes. For effectiveness, 82% of tasks completed error-free for the application and 70% for the clinical dashboard. For efficiency, tasks required an average 29 minutes to complete for the application and 20 minutes for the dashboard. SUS scores indicated excellent user satisfaction. This study identified key usability strengths, challenges, and areas for refinement of the ePRO system. Quantitative results showed high usability and user satisfaction, supported by qualitative insights highlighting specific issues and advantages. In response, targeted improvements were made, including refining welcome text, enhancing font readability, and updating the user manual. Overall, these findings demonstrate that the ePRO system is usable and acceptable to both patients and clinicians for symptom and quality-of-life monitoring in routine CAR-T care.

items.title: Pembrolizumab Activity in Tyrosine Kinase Inhibitor-Refractory Metastatic GIST: A Case Report.
items.abstract: Gastrointestinal stromal tumors (GISTs) are commonly driven by activating mutations in KIT or PDGFRA. Although sequential tyrosine kinase inhibitors (TKIs) have improved outcomes in advanced disease, acquired resistance is common. Prospective studies of immune checkpoint blockade in GIST have shown limited activity, and immunotherapy is not a standard treatment. A man diagnosed at age 57 with epithelioid small-bowel GIST developed hepatic metastatic disease 7 years after his initial diagnosis. His tumor harbored a primary KIT exon 11 D579del mutation, a secondary KIT exon 17 D820G mutation, and CDKN2A/CDKN2B deletions; available molecular testing reported a low tumor mutational burden (1 mutation/Mb) and microsatellite-stable disease. After progression or treatment-limiting toxicity during six TKI regimens, pembrolizumab was initiated on October 28, 2025, when he was 76 years old, and administered intravenously every 3 weeks. The treatment has demonstrated stable disease on CT imaging; cycle 13 was then administered on July 28, 2026. No treatment delays or treatment-related adverse events were reported through cycle 13. Pembrolizumab was associated with at least 9 months of disease control in TMB-low, microsatellite-stable metastatic GIST after six TKI regimens. Because contemporaneous immune profiling and complete historical dosing data were unavailable, this observation is hypothesis-generating and does not establish that prior TKI exposure sensitized the tumor to PD-1 blockade.

items.title: Expression Patterns of Histone Modification Regulators Predict Prognosis and Microenvironment Characteristics in Gastric Cancer.
items.abstract: Multiple studies have demonstrated a significant correlation between histone modifications and tumour initiation and progression. However, it remains unclear whether the histone modification profile contributes to the classification of patients with gastric cancer (GC). After analysing transcriptomic data from 76 histone modification regulators (HMR), we identified four distinct patterns in 838 GC specimens. These patterns demonstrated associations with different prognoses, treatment responses, biological pathways, and tumour microenvironment characteristics. Therefore, we used the Least Absolute Shrinkage and Selection Operator (LASSO) regression and multivariate Cox regression analysis to explore GC's histone modification regulator characteristics and established a 10-gene scoring scheme named "Histone Modification Regulator-based Risk Score (HR_score)" to cluster tumours into high- and low-risk subtypes. Patients with high scores are characterised by increased stromal cell infiltration and exhibit the activation of innate immunity. These observations may be linked to the immune-exclusion phenotype and a poor prognosis. Further analysis revealed a direct correlation between higher HR_score and diminished response to adjuvant chemotherapy and immunotherapy treatments. In summary, this study indicates that HR_score can serve as a robust prognostic tool for GC, which can effectively perform patient risk stratification and predict treatment response, providing potential value for guiding individualised treatment strategies.

items.title: IFNAR1 stabilization sustains CD8 + T cell persistence in IFN-high colorectal cancer liver metastases.
items.abstract: Colorectal cancer liver metastases (CRC-LMs) are associated with poor survival and frequently resist immunotherapy, yet the mechanisms underlying this immune refractoriness remain incompletely defined. Here, we identify a tumor-intrinsic type I interferon (IFN-I)-high state in CRC-LMs associated with loss of the IFN-α/β receptor subunit 1 (IFNAR1) on effector T lymphocytes within immune-enriched perimetastatic niches. Reduced IFNAR1 expression stratifies patients with poor clinical outcomes. Transcriptional profiling of patient-derived organoids and complementary preclinical models revealed heterogeneous but recurrent tumor-derived IFN-I production in CRC-LMs. In IFN-I high contexts, sustained signaling promoted IFNAR1 internalization on effector CD8 + T cells, impairing their persistence, survival, and effector function. Pharmacologic or genetic stabilization of IFNAR1 on cell surface restored CD8 + T cell fitness and selectively enhanced T cell receptor- and chimeric antigen receptor-based immunotherapies in IFN-I high tumors. These findings define a context-dependent IFN-I high / IFNAR1 low axis that constrains antitumor immunity in CRC-LMs and identify IFNAR1 stabilization as a strategy to convert chronic IFN signaling from a suppressive barrier into a therapeutic vulnerability.

items.title: Massively parallel self-assembly of suspendable microcompartments for functional cell screening.
items.abstract: Modern biology increasingly demands platforms that can compartmentalize and analyze single cells and cell-cell interactions at massive scale, yet existing compartmentalization strategies based on microfluidics suffer from critical limitations. Emerging lab-on-a-particle technologies such as nanovials enable anchored single cells or small groups of cells to be isolated and assayed in a fully suspendable and parallelized manner using standard instrumentation, although their open architectures can result in loss of growing or un-attached cells. Here, we introduce capped nanovials: self-assembling hydrogel compartments formed by docking spherical capping particles into bowl-shaped nanovials. We routinely achieve capping of >80% of all nanovials in a sample and >90% sorting yield by flow cytometry, making the capped nanovial system well-suited for preparing and running large-scale assays. Furthermore, we demonstrate stable clonal expansion of single mammalian, yeast, and bacterial cells; growth-based selections of >10,000 colonies; enhanced signal-to-noise in secretion assays; and high-purity selection of antibody-secreting cells based on activation of co-encapsulated T cell reporters (>30-fold signal, up to 100% selection purity). By combining the simplicity of a well plate with the functional precision of droplet microfluidics without requiring oil or custom instrumentation, capped nanovials realize accessible, high-throughput, and high-resolution experimentation.

items.title: Quantifying a Neglected Burden: Pregnancy-Associated Hepatocellular Carcinoma and Maternal Death in South Africa.
items.abstract: Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) during pregnancy is rare, with the literature confined to isolated case reports and small series. Women in sub-Saharan Africa (SSA) face disproportionate risk due to chronic hepatitis B virus (HBV) infection acquired perinatally, HCC in noncirrhotic livers at a young age, and fertility rates nearly three times those of Europe. To our knowledge, we report the largest cohort of pregnancy-associated HCC from SSA, drawn from a single South African center, and the first quantitative estimate of regional disparity versus Europe. Pregnant women with HCC at Groote Schuur Hospital, Cape Town, over 24 years (2001-2025) were identified from a prospectively maintained registry. A model integrating HCC incidence, age-at-diagnosis, fertility rates, and 1-year mortality compared the probability of pregnancy-associated HCC and maternal death in SSA versus Europe. Of the 728 registry patients, 192 (26.4%) were female and 10 (5.2%) were pregnant or within 1 year postpartum. The median age was 32.5 (IQR, 28.5-35.3), 70% had chronic HBV infection, and three had cirrhosis. Seven (70%) died, six within 90 days. Two patients survived beyond 10 years following curative resection. Four pregnancies ended in intrauterine fetal demise and five in live births. The modeled probability of pregnancy-associated HCC was 16 per 100,000 women in SSA versus 0.14 per 100,000 in Europe-a 114-fold difference-with a 187-fold greater risk of maternal death. Pregnancy-associated HCC in SSA is a quantifiable, preventable contributor to maternal mortality-nearly two orders of magnitude greater than in Europe. HBV endemicity, early-onset noncirrhotic HCC, and high fertility rates create a hostile environment for women of reproductive age. HBV-aware liver surveillance in antenatal care, strengthened prevention of mother-to-child transmission programs, and improved maternal mortality data systems are urgently needed.

items.title: Visceral leishmaniasis involving the kidney by direct infection and immune-mediated glomerulonephritis.
items.abstract: Leishmania are protozoan parasites that can infect the renal parenchyma and cause glomerular disease, in particular membranoproliferative glomerulonephritis, by immune-mediated mechanisms. Here, we present the case of a 50-year-old patient with a history of HIV infection, recurrent visceral leishmaniasis, past hepatitis C and previous illicit drug abuse. The patient presented with acute on chronic kidney injury and progressive proteinuria. Renal biopsy revealed interstitial nephritis and infection-related glomerulonephritis (IRGN) without membranoproliferative pattern. Leishmania parasites were detectable in interstitial macrophages, tubular epithelial cells and glomerular macrophages and confirmed by rabbit-anti-Leishmania- or rabbit-anti-CD1a-antibodies. Infected macrophages showed an M2-like phenotype. While interstitial nephritis and glomerular disease have been described in a few cases of visceral leishmaniasis, before, our case is remarkable for the presence of leishmanial amastigotes in glomerular macrophages and IRGN at the same time, adding to the spectrum of renal manifestations associated with leishmanial infection.

items.title: Disseminated histoplasmosis mimicking autoimmune hepatitis as a trigger of secondary hemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis in a pediatric patient.
items.abstract: Patients presenting with hemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis (HLH) are often critically ill, and rapid identification of both HLH and underlying triggers in secondary HLH is essential for successful treatment. We present a case of secondary HLH activated by disseminated histoplasmosis (DH) that mimicked autoimmune hepatitis (AIH) on liver histology and briefly led to an incorrect liver diagnosis. Once DH was identified, he was treated with antifungals in addition to HLH therapies and stabilized. He was subsequently found to have a heterozygous variant of uncertain significance in STAT1 . Our case is the first in the literature to describe liver biopsies in a pediatric patient who has DH that had triggered HLH, and due to striking histology that mimicked AIH, important to report.

items.title: Metagenomic study in a predominantly adult cohort with hepatitis of unknown etiology.
items.abstract: Hepatitis of unknown origin (HUO) remains a diagnostic challenge, with metagenomic studies underexplored in adult cohorts. This study characterized the plasma and fecal virome in a predominantly adult HUO cohort (48 adults and 1 adolescent). A total of 59 samples (44 plasma, 15 fecal) from 49 patients were subjected to ultra-multiplex targeted ribonucleic acid (RNA) sequencing (139 RNA viruses) and unbiased metagenomic sequencing. Targeted sequencing detected HCV in one plasma sample, confirmed by follow-up reverse transcription-polymerase chain reaction (RT-PCR) and seroconversion, leading to case reclassification. Metagenomic sequencing identified HBV sequences in another patient, along with sporadic goose circovirus (GoCV) and an unconfirmed low-level influenza A-like signal. Viral community analysis revealed distinct niche-specific profiles between plasma and feces. Overall, this exploratory study failed to identify a common pathogenic agent, underscoring the etiological heterogeneity of HUO. The detection of known hepatotropic viruses highlights the diagnostic value of metagenomic sequencing in complementing conventional serology and reclassifying some HUO cases. Larger controlled studies are warranted.

items.title: Mixed-Methods Analysis of a National Survey of Hospitals With Inpatient Hepatitis C Treatment Initiatives.
items.abstract: We surveyed clinicians about efforts to initiate hepatitis C antivirals during hospitalization or at discharge. We identified 29 hospitals in the United States working on such initiatives, with most efforts being less than 3 years old. Further initiative expansion is hindered by a lack of resources and uncertain insurance regulations.

items.title: Cancer Burden Among Adolescents and Young Adults in Guinea: A Retrospective Study From a National Referral Center, 2016-2023.
items.abstract: Adolescents and young adults (AYAs) exhibit a distinct cancer profile between pediatric and adult malignancies. Data from West Africa remain scarce, particularly in Guinea, where evidence is largely based on hospital data because of the absence of a structured cancer registry. This study aimed to describe the burden and profile of cancers among AYAs treated at the largest national referral hospital in Guinea. This was a retrospective descriptive study conducted from 2016 to 2023 in the oncology department of Donka University Hospital, Conakry. All AYAs (age 15-39 years) with histologically confirmed cancers were included. Sociodemographic and clinical data were collected from medical records, hospital registries, and the department's database. A total of 739 newly diagnosed AYAs were included, representing 27.7% of all histologically confirmed cancer cases. The number of cases increased from 28 in 2016 to 183 in 2023. The median age was 31 years (IQR, 26-35), and 71.2% were female. Breast cancer was the most common malignancy (38.2%), whereas lymphomas (15.0%) and liver cancers (12.2%) predominated among males. Sarcomas were the most common among 15- to 19-year-olds (44.4%). Overall, 58.9% were diagnosed at locally advanced stage and 27.7% were diagnosed with metastatic disease. Cancers among AYAs increased substantially over the study period in our context, with distinct age- and sex-related patterns. The predominance of advanced stages underscores ongoing challenges in early detection and access to care. These findings emphasize the need for strengthened cancer surveillance, earlier diagnosis strategies, and AYA-adapted supportive care in Guinea.

items.title: Prevalence, clinical characteristics, and etiologic spectrum of extremely low levels of high-density lipoprotein cholesterol in Thai patients: a single-center study.
items.abstract: Extremely low high-density lipoprotein cholesterol (HDL-C) is uncommon and may result from secondary conditions or rare genetic disorders. Data on persistently low HDL-C in Southeast Asians remain limited. We aim to determine the prevalence, clinical characteristics, underlying etiologies, and clinical outcomes of patients with persistent low HDL-C. This retrospective cohort study evaluated adults with persistently low HDL-C ( via laboratory and electronic medical records between January 2020 and December 2024. Patients were stratified into two phenotypes based on baseline HDL-C severity: markedly low (20-29 mg/dL) or extremely low (<20 mg/dL). Among 217,481 individuals undergoing lipid testing (1,053,662 HDL-C measurements), 164 patients had persistently low HDL-C (mean age, 56.9 years; 68.9% male). The prevalence of persistently low and extremely low HDL-C was 0.08% and 0.008%, respectively. Concomitant hypertriglyceridemia affected ∼75% of patients. Most cases were associated with secondary conditions. Extremely low HDL-C was more frequently associated with liver disease (41.2%) and active malignancy (29.4%), whereas metabolic syndrome predominated among patients with markedly low HDL-C (42.2%). During a median follow-up of 2.57 years, all-cause mortality was higher in the extremely low HDL-C group (29.4% vs. 11.6%; hazard ratio, 4.33; 95% CI, 1.58-11.91; p  = 0.004), while atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease rates were similar between groups (35.3% vs. 32.0%). Persistently low HDL-C is an exceedingly rare phenotype driven primarily by secondary systemic conditions. An extremely low HDL-C level appears to be a marker of severe underlying systemic illness and was associated with higher short-term mortality. Persistently low HDL-C is exceptionally rare and is predominantly associated with secondary systemic conditions, particularly hypertriglyceridemia, metabolic syndrome, liver disease, and malignancy.Extremely low HDL-C (<20 mg/dL) identifies a distinct high-risk phenotype, characterized by a greater association with liver disease and malignancy and a substantially higher all-cause mortality than HDL-C 20–29 mg/dL.Extremely low HDL-C should prompt systematic evaluation for underlying systemic illness rather than being viewed as an isolated lipid abnormality, with particular attention to liver disease, malignancy, hypertriglyceridemia, and metabolic disorders.

items.title: A Rare Form of Hepatocellular Carcinoma in a Patient With Crohn's Disease.
items.abstract: Fibrolamellar carcinoma (FLC) is a rare variant of hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) that affects people without underlying cirrhosis. The association between HCC and inflammatory bowel disease has been reported in patients with ulcerative colitis. A 23-year-old woman with newly diagnosed Crohn disease was incidentally found to have a large hepatic mass during evaluation of gastrointestinal symptoms. Imaging findings were concerning for HCC. Pathology after surgical resection revealed fibrolamellar variant of HCC. The patient developed recurrent FLC and underwent a portal lymphadenectomy and resection of a portal mass. She was started on lenvatinib and has remained in remission. Reports of HCC in patients with IBD are limited, and previously reported cases of FLC have occurred exclusively in patients with ulcerative colitis. We describe a case of FLC in a patient newly diagnosed with Crohn's disease. Although curative resection is possible, 50% to 100% of patients experience relapse and recurrence. This case highlights the characteristic clinical, radiographic, histopathologic, and molecular features of FLC and expands the limited literature on the association between FLC and IBD.
